correctness.rationale: The bridge heat vector obeys a directly derived cooperative two-state system with positive solution and characteristic polynomial \(\lambda^2-(m+3)\lambda+2\); its \(\ell^1\) total mass gives the claimed sharp two-exponential formula with sign-function extremizers. An explicit orthogonal-mode decomposition of any pendant-edge mass yields \(\ell^1\) amplitude bounds at decay rates 1,m+1,\(\lambda_-\),\(\lambda_+\). The elementary sup \(\sqrt t\,e^{-rt}\) formula makes the pendant time-weighted norm uniformly \(O(1)\). Positivity and eigenvalue asymptotics prove the global \(e^{-1/2}\sqrt m\) coefficient, while compactness and the unique maximizer of \(2\sqrt s\,e^{-2s}\) prove the location/time statement. Replayed verify.py independently computes finite graph heat vectors by Markov uniformization, passing 542 assertions. The infinite-family theorem is proved analytically, not inferred from these finite samples.

originality.rationale: The checked primary literature establishes curvature-conditioned gradient inequalities (Bauer et al., arXiv:1306.2561), positive-solution Hamilton-type spatial estimates (Horn), Lipschitz-input-to-Lipschitz-output curvature equivalences (Münch-Wojciechowski, arXiv:1712.00875), and a general abstract definition and consequences of optimal rough-input Lipschitz smoothing (De Ponti-Stefani, arXiv:2403.00620). None of the materially inspected theorem statements gives the exact bridge signed heat row, the sharp \(e^{-1/2}\sqrt m\) family norm, or the eventual optimizer edge/time. The scientific publication index returned graph-nearby results for a different bistar invariant, metric quantum pumpkin heat envelopes, and general spectral spacing; previously recorded mathematical claims concern finite paths, complete multipartite graphs, integer lattice heat time-derivatives and continuous metric stars, neither equivalent nor stronger on the family here. Residual search/priority risks are stated; lack of matching search hits alone is not a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Sharp \(L^\infty\)-to-edge-Lipschitz heat regularization is a natural stability invariant. On a canonical family of trees with fixed diameter three but increasing branching, the result supplies the precise degree-dependent obstruction to any dimension/degree-free \(t^{-1/2}\) smoothing bound for unnormalized graph Laplacians: coefficient \(e^{-1/2}\), a unique maximizing edge orbit for all sufficiently large m, and the asymptotically optimal diffusion time \(m/4\). The bridge sign extremizer and a uniform bound for all pendant edges turn the spectral slow mode into a true worst-case operator estimate; this spatially resolved sharp stability statement is not a routine renaming of the spectral gap or an arbitrary numerical slice.
